resources.string: Fast mode follows each source’s interval with a permanent notification. Android 15+ may stop it after 6 hours in the background; automatic checks then continue. Battery saving can delay both modes.

Automatic checks run at least 15 minutes apart, including after a reboot. Android can delay them. Fast mode uses the intervals you set below. A first successful check records existing items without notifying you.
Keep an eye on what matters
Add an RSS feed, GitHub repository, discussion, Sponsors profile or YouTube video to get notified about new activity.
Check the source format and use an interval between 5 and 604800 seconds.
Invalid configuration. No settings were changed.
You can add up to 50 sources.
Notifications are disabled. Allow them to receive alerts; new items are kept pending.
Tap to view sources · stop to return to automatic checks
Fast mode could not start. Automatic checks remain available.
New notifications will appear here. The first check quietly records items already present in your sources.
The 200 most recent notifications. Tap an item to open its link.
Clear notification history? Monitoring state is kept.
This item has no web link.
No application can open this web link.

GitHub discussions and Sponsors require a token (Sponsors also requires read:user). YouTube requires a YouTube Data API v3 key. Credentials are encrypted on this device and excluded from exports and Android backups.
Credentials could not be decrypted or saved. Enter them again.

Import a desktop config.json or an Android export. Empty desktop examples are skipped. Exports include source addresses, which may contain private RSS tokens; keep the file private. API credentials and history are not exported.
Replace the current sources with %1$d imported sources? Their first check will establish a new baseline.
The file could not be read or written.

Only notify me about questions concerning local storage…

Write a rule for this source, or leave it empty to notify everything. With a rule, the title, author and up to 4000 characters of text are sent to Claude Haiku. Each new item uses a paid API call, separate from a Claude subscription. Rejected items are remembered. If Claude is unavailable, the item is still notified with a warning.
Claude key missing: items will be notified without filtering. Add the key in Settings.
AI filter unavailable · notified without filtering
Claude key missing · notified without filtering
%1$d items rejected by the AI filter
Scan the QR displayed by watch2notif on your PC

Connect both devices to the same local network. On the PC, click Send to phone. Scan its QR within 2 minutes. Sources, Claude rules and API keys are transferred encrypted, once; the PC then closes access. Keys remain encrypted on your phone.
Import %1$d sources and %2$d API keys from your PC? Current sources will be replaced. Keys missing from the PC will be kept on this phone. The first check records existing items quietly.
Sources and API keys imported from the PC
Invalid QR or encrypted configuration. Nothing was imported.
This QR has expired or was already used. Generate a new one on the PC.
Cannot reach the PC. Check the shared local network, VPN and PC firewall, then generate a new QR.
The PC did not respond in time. Check the shared Wi-Fi network and PC firewall, then generate a new QR.
The PC refused the connection. Keep the PC transfer window open and generate a new QR.
The PC returned HTTP %1$d. Generate a new QR and try again.
Authentication refused (HTTP 401). Check the saved credential.
Access refused (HTTP 403). Check permissions, API activation and quota.
Service rate limit reached (HTTP 429). Try again later.
Tests enabled sources with saved credentials. Also makes one short paid Claude API request if a key or AI filter is configured. Results stay on screen; monitoring history is preserved.
Updates come from GitHub releases. The download and application signature are verified before Android asks you to confirm installation. Your sources and encrypted keys are kept.
